research_updates.notes: Source families checked: IM3 inventory geometry and provenance; Markley current and archived operator pages; Lowell assessor parcel P90290/MBLU 184/4765/2; 2015, 2018, 2020, 2023 and 2024 City planning and bond records; deed/sale fields; and web archives. research_updates.title: Investment, incentive and fiscal audit — forecasts separated from cumulative observations
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: the 2015 EACC approval release; City TIF summaries and FY2020-FY2026 budgets; the 2023 preliminary official statement; EDIP awardee, annual-report, compliance and decertification pages; City Council agendas, minutes and attachments; assessor history; Treasurer/Collector billing; municipal audits/ACFRs, capital plans and check-register/vendor searches; and official-statement debt disclosures for 2015-2026. Queries used Markley, Markley Group LLC, Markley Boston LLC, 2 Prince Avenue, 1 Markley Way, P90290, 184/4765/2, 2015-2035 TIF and EDIP. FY2020 records execution in May 2015, and the 2017 summary identifies a clawback and Middlesex 3 membership; the signed agreement, payment schedule and annual compliance ledger were not located. The fragment retains the $72.8 million Phase I plan, $104,121,860 cumulative-investment observation, $77,182,505 combined local incentive forecast, $187,500 approved state credit, $1,624,655.79 cumulative real-estate TIF savings and a separate $534,231.97 FY2026 real-property bill. Adopted-budget documents 20496, 23767, 26555 and proposed-budget document 30950 have no Markley row. InvoiceCloud returned all four FY2026 real-property quarters with zero balances, but billed tax is not cash received and the portal does not identify payment versus adjustment; partial FY2025/FY2027 displays are excluded, and the personal-property query returned no open invoice, which cannot establish historical liability or exemption value. Fiscal candidate decisions: an annual-receipt or net-fiscal model is rejected because recipient distributions, cash collections, realized personal-property relief and same-scope public costs are missing; a statutory TIF counterfactual is rejected because the executed schedule and annual baseline are absent. The sole eligible public-cost candidate reuses the exact FY2026 bill only as the same-account $534,231.97 service-cost break-even identity. It is decision-relevant and reproducible but is neither observed cost nor a surplus/deficit and must not be summed with the bill.

research_updates.title: Operations and workforce audit — dated headcounts and local-resident subset added
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Lowell TIF tables and annual certified-project reports; Massachusetts EDIP annual-report, compliance and decertification material; Markley careers, staff and facility pages; job boards; customer and tenant records; workforce-development, apprenticeship, local-hiring and wage-enforcement searches; and state procurement records for 2015-2026. Exact City/EDIP searches found dated Markley rows for 2019, December 2020 and December 31, 2025 but no public 2021-2024 annual certified-employment table. The account retains 26 employees in 2019, 31 in December 2020 and 101 full-time permanent employees at the Lowell location on December 31, 2025, including a non-additive subset of 30 Lowell residents. The 2025 report also lists 29 hires during that year, but the available metric is a stock and the hire flow stays in source metadata. The State ITS86 listing makes Markley Boston LLC contract-eligible and states a supplier-diversity commitment, but it does not disclose a Lowell-facility procurement payment and contributes no amount. No annual-average FTE, occupation table, wage, payroll, hours, apprenticeship outcome, contractor/customer headcount, turnover, county-resident total, procurement payment or selected-building employment was found.

research_updates.title: Resource, utility and environmental audit — permit equipment added; consumption remains unallocated
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: MassDEP air-plan applications, notices and OADR decisions under 24-AQ02F-0001-APP/NE-25-002, including the March 27, 2026 final decision and July 2026 reconsideration docket; Lowell Planning Board, Sustainability Council, water, sewer and data-center materials; fuel-storage licensing; National Grid and Massachusetts DPU dockets and tariffs; ISO New England queue and reliability material; EPA facility searches; Markley facility, PPA and sustainability pages; and 2025-2026 reporting based on water bills or operator statements. The permit-listed facility total of 27 emergency generators is retained, distinct from installation and operation. The City authorized four 6,000-gallon diesel tanks in July 2025; a later fuel-license amendment application filed September 8 was withdrawn October 13, so no additional capacity is inferred. Licensed tank capacity is not fuel inventory or use and the vocabulary has no matching storage-capacity metric. AP reports an operator-stated summer peak of about 118,000 gallons per day, but no meter ledger or annual total was published and the vocabulary has no direct actual peak-water metric. A Markley solar PPA covers a broader company purchase in Eversource territory and is not allocated to the National Grid-served Lowell site. No facility annual electricity, demand, tariff payment, grid-upgrade cost, verified annual water/wastewater, generator runtime, fuel use, actual emissions or selected-building resource series was found.

research_updates.title: Community-recipient audit — one recipient-verified Lowell contribution added
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: University of Massachusetts Lowell, Middlesex Community College, Greater Lowell Community Foundation, Merrimack Valley Food Bank, Lowell Public Schools, youth sports, libraries, housing and other food-assistance recipients; City packets; Markley press and social pages; and local news archives for grants, sponsorships, donations, STEM, education and volunteer support from 2015-2026. Queries combined Markley or Markley Group with each recipient and contribution term. UMass Lowell lists Markley Group in the $25,000 Signature Sponsor tier for the May 1-2, 2026 Meehan Student Center dedication. The event's more-than-$300,000 total is not attributed to Markley. A separate recipient page verifies a $25,000 2025 Merrimack Valley Food Bank gift; no complete annual Middlesex County grant register, in-kind valuation, volunteer-hour series or campus-attributable total was found. Community-model candidate: annualizing, averaging or extrapolating the two gifts is rejected because they are distinct episodic transfers, the recipient universe is incomplete and neither is allocated to the campus or selected building.

research_updates.title: County-outcome eligibility audit — GDP, employment and wages rejected separately
research_updates.notes: The repository county economic panels for 2001-2024, study-county exclusions, inventory history and the direct evidence above were reviewed with a November 2015 opening anchor and 2007-2014 candidate pre-period. Markley is not Middlesex County's first known data-center operation: the governed first-entry evidence documents earlier colocation in Somerville, while Markley's 2018-2026 expansions prevent a single stable post-treatment boundary. GDP candidate: difference-in-differences, event-study and synthetic-control designs are rejected because exposure predates the anchor, treatment intensity changes and no defensible unexposed donor design or project allocation is available; a descriptive benchmark gap is also rejected as insufficiently decision-relevant because it cannot distinguish Markley from Middlesex County's large, diverse economy. Employment candidate: the same identification failures apply, and the 26, 31 and 101 facility snapshots neither measure county employment change nor define annual-average FTE. Wage candidate: the same identification failures apply, no project payroll or occupation mix was found, and nominal county average weekly wages would mix industry composition and inflation. Each outcome therefore remains an explicit gap; no descriptive comparison is presented as causal. No records requests or other solicitations were made.

research_updates.title: Corrective investment and construction model screen — direct records remain non-additive
research_updates.notes: Gap-closure searches covered Lowell Planning Board applications, drawing sets, stormwater reports, staff memoranda, minutes and conditions for 2015, 2018, 2020, 2023 and 2024; Inspectional Services monthly issued-permit files for January 2024-June 2026; CSS online permitting and City outage guidance; permit IDs BLD202400574, ELC202406426, BLD202413857, ELC202507553 and BLD202603584; contractors Willard L. Cleveland, New England Electric Group, Coordinated Systems Consulting, Saiful Bouquet and Stantec; and operator, trade and archive searches under both addresses and parcel P90290. The 2024 memorandum confirms proposed equipment and utility work but supplies no expenditure or completion amount. Investment candidate: annualizing the $104,121,860 cumulative FY2020-labeled observation or allocating it to the selected building is rejected because its expenditure dates, asset mix and building allocation are unknown. Construction candidate: summing permit valuations or applying construction multipliers is rejected because the amounts are administrative estimates with unresolved building/trade overlap, no audited spend, no equipment exclusion, no duration, no worker/payroll input and no local-purchase share. The approximately $200 million campus forecast and $72.8 million Phase I plan remain forecasts and cannot replace those missing inputs.

research_updates.title: Corrective supplier and operations model screen — eligibility is not evidence of payment
research_updates.notes: Supplier and procurement searches covered COMMBUYS and ITS86 under Markley Boston LLC and master blanket PO-26-1080-OSD03-OSD03-39704; City vendor/check-register, capital-budget and council-payment searches under Markley, the named construction firms and the two site addresses; contractor portfolios; operator customer/career pages; Massachusetts workforce, apprenticeship and wage-enforcement sources; and archived job listings for 2015-2026. ITS86 confirms only contract eligibility and a 3 percent supplier-diversity commitment, not a purchase order, invoice, Lowell performance location or payment. Supplier candidate: applying a transferred local-purchase share or indirect multiplier is rejected because no vendor payment base, geography, timing or non-overlap evidence exists. Household-spending candidate is rejected because construction and operating payroll are absent. Operations candidate: interpolating 2019, 2020 and 2025 headcount snapshots or multiplying them by county/occupation wages is rejected because the stocks are not annual-average FTE, roles and compensation are unknown, the Lowell-resident count is only a nested subset, contractors/customers are not measured and no selected-building allocation exists.

research_updates.title: Corrective utility, environmental, infrastructure and legal-financing screen
research_updates.notes: Searches covered MEPA archive and Environmental Monitor entry EEA 15988; Massachusetts EEA facility/permit search; MassDEP application 24-AQ02F-0001-APP, approval NE-25-002 and OADR 2025-022 decisions; EPA facility indexes; Lowell water, wastewater, stormwater, fuel-license and Sustainability Council files; National Grid/Massachusetts Electric dockets, tariffs and project materials; Massachusetts DPU and ISO New England indexes; operator PPA/sustainability pages; registry/deed references Book 29147/Page 49; City budgets, ACFRs, official statements, bond/TIF/PILOT/IRB and legal-agreement files; and public financing searches for Markley Group LLC, Markley Boston LLC, 1 Markley Way and 2 Prince Avenue over 2015-2026. EEA 15988 directly ties a fully constructed 23-kV line project to Markley's load but gives no cost, customer contribution, subsidy, demand or selected-building allocation and says no Commonwealth financial assistance was sought. Resource candidate: converting the 50-MW approval-stage plan into annual electricity or the reported 118,000-gallon summer peak into annual water is rejected because neither is metered annual use, operating capacity is unverified, load/cooling factors are absent and all figures are campus-wide. Infrastructure-cost and financing candidates are rejected because EEA 15988, the air docket, the deed, City debt files and searched TIF materials disclose no compatible project cost, payment, borrower balance or allocation. Permit limits and equipment counts are not emissions, fuel use or public cost.

source.title: EEA No. 15988 — Markley Data Center and 2385 Line Maintenance Project, Notice of Project Change certificate

source.notes: The MEPA certificate identifies Massachusetts Electric Company d/b/a National Grid as proponent of upgrades to 23-kV line 2385 to support Markley's electrical load and area reliability. It says the original three-phase project was fully constructed, including 189 replaced utility poles, a 3,950-circuit-foot extension from Wigginville Substation to the data center and other Lowell/Billerica/Tewksbury work; the change added ten poles. The project sought no Commonwealth financial assistance. The record supplies no project cost, cost-allocation, customer contribution, electricity use, demand, tariff payment or public subsidy and cannot be allocated to the selected IM3 building.

research_updates.notes: The Merrimack Valley Food Bank site was searched by Markley and Markley Group for 2015-2026 and opened the recipient-hosted November 2025 report. research_updates.title: GDP source review — county series cannot identify the project
research_updates.notes: BEA annual county real-GDP files and the repository's 2001-2024 governed panel were reviewed for FIPS 25017, with a candidate 2007-2014 pre-period, 2015 opening anchor and exclusion of all study counties from possible donors. The series is available, but the causal and descriptive candidates are rejected for the project-specific reasons recorded in the county-outcome eligibility audit: earlier Middlesex data-center activity, changing Markley exposure after 2015, concurrent county shocks, no selected-building allocation and inadequate decision relevance for an unattributed descriptive gap.

source.title: BEA Regional data — annual county real GDP through 2024
source.notes: The repository's governed county panel was checked for Middlesex County annual real GDP over 2001-2024 and for non-study comparison counties. The official county series is usable as descriptive context, but it contains all county activity and cannot identify Markley Lowell; earlier county colocation activity and continuing Markley expansions prevent a clean 2015 treatment boundary.

research_updates.title: Employment and wage source review — county context stays non-causal
research_updates.notes: BLS QCEW county employment and nominal average-weekly-wage files and the repository's 2001-2024 governed panel were reviewed for FIPS 25017, with the same candidate 2007-2014 pre-period, 2015 opening anchor and study-county donor exclusion. Employment and wage comparisons are each rejected: the county series do not measure Markley FTE, payroll, occupations or compensation; prior data-center exposure and later campus phases defeat a stable treatment; and nominal wage changes mix inflation and county industry composition. No county gap is labeled or published as a facility effect.

source.notes: The repository's governed county panel was checked for Middlesex County employment and nominal average weekly wages over 2001-2024 and for non-study comparison counties. No positive or negative net fiscal result is asserted.
modeled_syntheses.notes: Conditional assessed-liability threshold only. Equality marks break-even against the FY2026 bill; actual costs and collections are unknown, so the estimate must not be summed with the underlying tax claim or presented as a fiscal surplus.
